title: Story verification judges CI with the merge gate's evidence rules
background: Story verification (US-26.4.2, US-26.4.3) has never produced a CI verdict in production: its worker passed an uncast UUID to a schemaless query, so every run that had a commit crashed before reaching CI. Its CI read also used the check-runs endpoint, which a fine-grained token cannot reach (#913). PR #914, then #915, fixed both and kept finding, round after round, that the subsystem's rules were never designed: which runs count as the commit's CI, which repository is read and with whose credential, and when a missing, pending or unreachable answer means wait rather than give up. #915 was held after its third review round; its review threads are the record of every edge found. The thread merge gate (US-45.6) already answers all three questions for a thread checkpoint, with rules hardened over three review rounds of its own.

story.i_want_to: have story verification record a CI verdict by the same rules the merge gate uses
story.so_that: a verification run means what a merge decision means, instead of a second, weaker reading of the same CI

rationale: Two readings of one commit's CI that can disagree are worse than one. Reusing Loopctl.Delivery.CiEvidence settles which runs count (the intake source's required_checks, by job name) and reusing the merge gate's transient-versus-final handling settles when to wait, so verification designs neither again.

acceptance_criteria.description: The worker resolves the story's repository ONLY from its project's intake source (Loopctl.Intake.source_for_project/2), never from projects.repo_url, for the CI read AND for the local fallback's clone. A project without exactly one live intake source records ci_unavailable_reason no_intake_source and reads nothing.

The verdict is Loopctl.Delivery.CiEvidence.judge/2 over the intake source's required_checks: pass only when every required job name concluded success, fail when one failed, wait while one is pending. A source with no required_checks records no_required_checks and reads nothing.
The worker's schemaless story/project query casts its UUID parameters, so a run with a commit reaches the CI read (the crash #914 found).

Transient forge failures (timeouts, connection errors, 5xx, rate limits) are waited out the way the merge gate treats unevaluated reads; a run ends as error only after verification_max_run_age_seconds from its creation. The CiBehaviour contract declares the waiting outcome rather than the worker matching one adapter's error terms.
An abbreviated commit SHA is resolved to the full object id once, and the full id is persisted on the run.

Every GitHub read goes through one credential seam, so the per-tenant credential decision in #915 changes that seam and nothing else. Reads carry the operator GITHUB_TOKEN until that decision is made.
ac_results records the CI verdict's evidence URL on pass or fail, and on no verdict a short reason code that never contains a URL or a repository name.

test_cases.name: repo_url is never read
preconditions: a project whose repo_url names another repository than its intake source
steps: run verification with a stub that fails on any request outside the intake source's repository
expected_results: only the intake source's repository is read

test_cases.name: required checks decide
steps: a commit whose unrelated workflow succeeded and whose test job is pending, then failed, then succeeded
expected_results: wait, then fail, then pass; the unrelated success never passes it

test_cases.name: transient failure waits, age ends it
steps: answer 502, then a timeout, then a run older than the age window

test_cases.name: abbreviated SHA and recorded evidence
preconditions: a run recorded with a 7-character SHA
expected_results: one commit read in total; the run carries the full SHA and the failing job's URL

technical_notes: Reuse GitHubPullRequestSource's workflow-run and jobs readers; the branch-free read #915 added (commit_ci_runs) is the starting point, with jobs read per newest run as check_evidence/3 does.
Mutation-test the wiring as well as the rule: the repository source, the required_checks lookup, the cast, and the wait arms.
#915's review threads list every edge found; each must be a test here or be removed by the design.
